<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

MachineHealthCheck reconciliation now annotates standard and spot MHCs with their parent NodePool. NodePool reconciliation maps a false `RemediationAllowed` condition to `Ready=False`, preserving its reason and message. MHC watch events are filtered to relevant changes in remediation status, reason, or message while retaining hosted-cluster scoping. Unit tests cover annotations, readiness propagation, and predicate behavior.

### Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant MachineHealthCheck
  participant NodePoolController
  participant NodePool
  MachineHealthCheck->>NodePoolController: update RemediationAllowed
  NodePoolController->>MachineHealthCheck: inspect condition
  MachineHealthCheck-->>NodePoolController: return status, reason, message
  NodePoolController->>NodePool: set Ready=False with MHC details
```

**Suggested reviewers:** `clebs`, `nirshal`, `bryan-cox`

</details>

>## Summary
>
>- Bubble up the CAPI MachineHealthCheck `RemediationAllowed` condition into the NodePool `Ready` condition. When `RemediationAllowed=False` (too many unhealthy machines exceed `maxUnhealthy`), the NodePool `Ready` condition is overridden to `False` with reason `TooManyUnhealthy` and the MHC's original message preserved.
>- Add a MachineHealthCheck watch with a predicate filter so only `RemediationAllowed` condition changes (Status, Reason, or Message) trigger NodePool reconciliation, avoiding unnecessary reconciliations from unrelated MHC status field updates.
>- Set `nodePoolAnnotation` on the MHC so the existing `enqueueParentNodePool` watch handler can map MHC events back to the parent NodePool.
>
>## Test plan
>
>- [x] `TestMHCRemediationAllowedBubbledUpToReady` — verifies Ready is overridden when RemediationAllowed=False, left untouched when True or absent
>- [x] `TestMHCRemediationAllowedChangedPredicate` — verifies predicate filters Update events correctly (8 cases: Status changes, Reason-only change, Message-only change, condition appearing/disappearing, no-change cases)
>- [x] `TestReconcileMachineHealthCheckAnnotation` — verifies nodePoolAnnotation is set on MHC
>- [x] Full nodepool controller test suite passes
>- [x] `make verify` passes (lint, gitlint, CRD schema check)

CNTRPLANE-400 Validation Summary

  What was tested

  ```
The fix bubbles up MachineHealthCheck (MHC) RemediationAllowed=False condition with reason TooManyUnhealthy to the NodePool's Ready condition, giving operators visibility when
  auto-repair is blocked.

  Test environment

  - Management cluster: ROSA HCP (us-east-1)
  - HO image: quay.io/sminonne/hypershift:[CNTRLPLANE-400](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CNTRLPLANE-400)-*** (contains the fix)
  - CPO image: quay.io/sminonne/hypershift-cpo:cntrlplane-400-compat-***
  - Release: 4.21.15 GA
  - Hosted cluster: *** with 2 replicas, autoRepair=true

  Test 1: TooManyUnhealthy condition bubbles up

  1. Paused CAPI MHC reconciler via cluster.x-k8s.io/paused annotation
  2. Patched MHC status: RemediationAllowed=False, reason=TooManyUnhealthy
  3. Result: NodePool Ready condition immediately changed to:
    - Status: False
    - Reason: TooManyUnhealthy
    - Message: Remediation is not allowed, the number of unhealthy machines exceeds maxUnhealthy (total: 2, unhealthy: 3, maxUnhealthy: 2)

  Test 2: Recovery when condition clears

  1. Patched MHC status back to: RemediationAllowed=True
  2. Result: NodePool Ready condition immediately recovered to:
    - Status: True
    - Reason: AsExpected

  Conclusion

  The CNTRPLANE-400 fix works as designed. The HO's nodepool controller correctly watches MHC conditions via the mhcRemediationAllowedChangedPredicate and bubbles up the TooManyUnhealthy
   reason and message to the NodePool's Ready condition.
```
